newsitem.title: UK: Thorn says will continue U.S. legal defence.
newsitem.headline: Thorn says will continue U.S. legal defence.

text.p: British-based electronic goods retailer Thorn Plc said on Monday it would continue to vigorously defend its rental-purchase sales system from legal action in some parts of the United States.

In a statement with its debut interim results, chief executive Mike Metcalf said Thorn was considering an appeal submission in the state of Minnesota, following an earlier move to appeal in Wisconsin, and would contest any court decisions, such as one in Pennsylvania, to award damages against it.
"In view of this, it is not currently possible to estimate with reasonable accuracy what provision (if any) might be required in respect of these cases," he said.
Thorn has said in the past it would not expect any damages to be material to shareholders' funds.
It has respectively eight, 23 and 46 stores in Minnesota, Wisconsin and Pennsylvania out of a total of 1,316 owned stores in the U.S.
Thorn's U.S. sales, which grew 14 percent in the six months to September 30, accounted for 35 percent of the company's turnover.
These states have taken issue with the way Thorn prices and markets its rental-purchase sales, claiming they should be regulated in the same way as consumer credit transactions.
Thorn noted that legislation already exists in 43 states which distinguishes rental-purchases from consumer credit.
